# a5view

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/belian-earth/a5view/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/belian-earth/a5view/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

Interactive map viewer for [A5](https://a5geo.org) geospatial cells, powered by [deck.gl](https://deck.gl) over a [MapLibre](https://maplibre.org) basemap. Renders cells directly in the browser with deck.gl's A5Layer and [a5-js](https://github.com/felixpalmer/a5); no pre-computation of boundaries needed. Intentionally minimal API for fast prototyping and exploration of A5 data.

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("belian-earth/a5view")
```

a5view 0.3.0 draws [A5 1.0](https://github.com/felixpalmer/a5/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) cell ids, as produced by a5R >= 0.9.9.9000. Ids written by earlier versions of a5R are valid 1.0 cells in the wrong place, so a5view cannot tell them apart and draws them where 1.0 puts them; convert them once with `a5R::a5_migrate()`. Use a5view 0.2.x for pre-1.0 ids.

## Usage

```{r example, screenshot.opts = list(delay = 3)}
library(a5R)
library(a5view)

# Pick a cell and expand to a disk
cell <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(-3.19, 55.95, resolution = 9)
disk <- a5_grid_disk(cell, k = 10) |>
  a5_uncompact(resolution = 9)

# Colour by distance from centre
a5_view(disk, fill = a5_cell_distance(cell, disk), palette = "Inferno")
```

Features:

- Colour mapping from numeric vectors or data frame columns with any `hcl.colors()` palette, with an on-map legend
- Basemaps from [OpenFreeMap](https://openfreemap.org) (dark, light, OSM; no API key) and Esri satellite imagery, with an interactive selector; map labels render above the cells
- Opacity slider, zoom/compass control, scale bar
- Hover tooltip with the cell id, fill value and any extra columns (`tooltip = c("col1", "col2")`); click to pin a cell; nothing shows over empty map
- Cell border styling
- 3D extrusion via `elevation`
- Globe projection (`globe = TRUE`)
- Precomputed level-of-detail pyramids for large datasets (`aggregate = "rep_child"` / `"mean"`), streamed to the browser as parquet and decoded per viewport; inside Shiny the file is served with HTTP range requests so only the row groups in view are transferred
- Shiny bindings (`a5_viewOutput` / `renderA5_view`) and in-place updates via `a5_view_update()`
- Optional polygon-draw toolbar (`draw_polygon = TRUE`) for selecting an
  area of interest

## ggplot2

`geom_a5()` draws cells in ggplot2, alongside `geom_sf()` layers and in any `coord_sf()` projection. Large cell sets are drawn as a raster at the output resolution, so a plot of millions of cells costs about the same as one of thousands.

The package ships `s2_santiago`, 15,626 resolution-18 cells (about 22 m across) of a [cloud-free Sentinel-2 mosaic](https://source.coop/earthgenome/sentinel2-temporal-mosaics) over Parque O'Higgins in Santiago, Chile. Mapping the red, green and blue bands through `cells_rgb()` gives a true-colour composite; its output is already colour, so no scale is needed.

```{r ggplot-rgb, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6.5, dpi = 150}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(s2_santiago, aes(cell = cell, fill = cells_rgb(B04, B03, B02, range = c(300, 2800)))) +
  geom_a5() +
  labs(title = "Sentinel-2 true colour, Santiago 2023")
```

Any fill scale works, and `coord_sf()` reprojects the cells, here NDVI in UTM zone 19S:

```{r ggplot-utm, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6, dpi = 150}
ggplot(s2_santiago, aes(cell = cell, fill = (B08 - B04) / (B08 + B04))) +
  geom_a5() +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greens", direction = 1, name = "NDVI") +
  coord_sf(crs = 32719) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Sentinel-2 mosaic by Earth Genome (CC-BY 4.0). Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2023.

## Polygon draw mode (Shiny only)

Setting `draw_polygon = TRUE` adds a draw-polygon toggle to the toolbar.
Clicks place vertices, a double-click closes the polygon, and the
result is sent to Shiny as a WKT string at `input$<id>_polygon_draw`.
The widget itself does not visualise which cells fall inside the
polygon — the canonical pattern is to resolve the WKT server-side and
update the map fills via `a5_view_update()`. Outside Shiny there is no
input listener, so the feature has no effect.

```r
a5_viewOutput("map")

# server
output$map <- renderA5_view({
  a5_view(my_cells, draw_polygon = TRUE)
})

observeEvent(input$map_polygon_draw, {
  cells_in_poly <- a5R::a5_polygon_to_cells(
    wk::wkt(input$map_polygon_draw),
    resolution = 4L
  ) |>
    a5R::a5_uncompact()
  # ... use cells_in_poly, e.g. a5_view_update() with selection-driven fills.
})
```

See `inst/examples/polygon-select/app.R` for a complete demo combining
single-cell click selection with polygon-based selection.
